items.label: f02-retry-model
items.front: How does a failed step get retried in FlowForge?
items.back: In the worker catch: attempts = job.attempts + 1. If attempts < maxAttempts (maxRetries + 1), markStepRetrying resets the same job row to AVAILABLE with readyAt = now + attempts * 15 s and the step to RETRYING, in one transaction. Otherwise the step is marked failed and the job dead.

items.label: f07-json-fields-fail-before-request
items.front: What happens when a step's config text in the builder is not valid JSON?
items.back: The save mutation's mutationFn builds the payload first, and parseJsonField throws "Step N config must contain valid JSON." while doing so. The throw rejects the mutation before any request is sent, React Query calls onError, and setFormError puts that sentence in the form's red error line. The server's schema never sees the bad value.

items.label: f04-schedule-race
items.front: How can one scheduled tick produce two runs?
items.back: The scheduler loop and the internal dispatch route can run dispatchScheduledRuns concurrently; it reads due workflows, enqueues, then advances nextScheduledAt with no lock. Fix: claim with a conditional update on nextScheduledAt and enqueue only if one row changed.

items.label: f06-internal-token-guard
items.front: How are the internal scheduler and worker routes authenticated?
items.back: They declare no user permission. Inside the handler, assertInternalToken compares the x-internal-token header with INTERNAL_WORKER_TOKEN using a plain !== (not constant-time): missing or wrong gives 401 INVALID_INTERNAL_TOKEN. If the env var is unset it throws a plain Error instead of an AppError. Machine auth is kept apart from user sessions on purpose.

items.label: f05-run-creation-transaction
items.front: What does createRunForWorkflow write, and why in one transaction?
items.back: A QUEUED run, one PENDING step-run per step, a single job row for the first step only, and a workflow.run.created audit row, all inside one $transaction. The job table is the queue, so enqueueing commits with the run: there is never a run without its first job, or a job without its run. Later steps get their jobs from the worker as each step finishes.

items.label: f01-execute-route
items.front: In what order does executeRoute handle a request, and how are errors mapped?
items.back: Load the session actor; if the route needs a permission, 401 without an actor, then assertPermission (403); then parse the body; then run the handler. AppError keeps its status; anything else (ZodError, SyntaxError, Prisma errors) becomes a generic 500 and is not logged.

items.label: f03-lease-gap
items.front: Why can a run stay RUNNING forever, and what is the fix?
items.back: The lease query only takes AVAILABLE rows, so a job leased by a worker that died stays LEASED. Fix: also select LEASED rows whose leasedUntil < NOW(), and check leaseToken when completing so a slow worker cannot finish a job re-leased to someone else.

items.prompt: A step condition says context.riskScore lt 50, but no earlier step ever wrote riskScore. Does the step run?

choices.text: No: a missing path makes every comparison in the rule false
Yes: the missing value reads as null, and Number(null) is 0
No: a missing value is NaN, and NaN is never below 50
Yes: conditions are skipped for keys that are not present

choices: No: a missing path makes every comparison in the rule false
Yes: the missing value reads as null, and Number(null) is 0
No: a missing value is NaN, and NaN is never below 50
Yes: conditions are skipped for keys that are not present

items.explanation: readPath returns null for a missing segment; lt compares Number(null) < Number(50), which is 0 < 50, so the rule matches and the step runs.

items.prompt: A worker leases a job and then its process is killed. The lease was for 30 seconds. What happens to the job afterwards?

choices.text: It is reset to AVAILABLE by the scheduler on its next tick
It stays LEASED, as leasing only takes AVAILABLE rows
After 30 s another worker leases it again under a new token
It is marked dead once leasedUntil has passed without work

choices: It is reset to AVAILABLE by the scheduler on its next tick
It stays LEASED, as leasing only takes AVAILABLE rows
After 30 s another worker leases it again under a new token
It is marked dead once leasedUntil has passed without work

items.explanation: leaseNextAvailableJob selects status = 'AVAILABLE' AND readyAt <= NOW(); nothing turns an expired LEASED row back into AVAILABLE, so the run stays RUNNING.

items.prompt: An hourly SCHEDULE workflow was due at 01:00, 02:00 and 03:00, but the scheduler was down until 03:30. What happens on its first tick?

choices.text: No run is created; the missed ticks are simply skipped
Three runs are created, one for each missed interval
Three runs are created and the next time is 04:00
One run is created, and the next time is set from 03:30

choices: No run is created; the missed ticks are simply skipped
Three runs are created, one for each missed interval
Three runs are created and the next time is 04:00
One run is created, and the next time is set from 03:30

items.explanation: dispatchScheduledRuns enqueues once per due workflow, then sets nextScheduledAt with getNextScheduledAt(cron, now), so missed ticks collapse into one catch-up run.

items.prompt: An operator manually triggers their own workflow while it is PAUSED. What is the response?

choices.text: 403, as a paused workflow is locked to admins
201, as a manual trigger also works when paused
409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE; only ACTIVE ones can run
422, as paused workflows must be republished first

choices: 403, as a paused workflow is locked to admins
201, as a manual trigger also works when paused
409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE; only ACTIVE ones can run
422, as paused workflows must be republished first

items.explanation: After the scoped load and the ownership check, triggerWorkflowManually throws 409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE for any status other than ACTIVE.

items.prompt: An operator saves a workflow whose step name is one character long, below the schema's min(2). What does the API return?

choices.text: 500 with "An unexpected server error occurred."
422 with a WORKFLOW_STEP_REQUIRED code
400, with each of the zod field errors in the response
201, as step names are not validated yet

choices: 500 with "An unexpected server error occurred."
422 with a WORKFLOW_STEP_REQUIRED code
400, with each of the zod field errors in the response
201, as step names are not validated yet

items.explanation: bodySchema.parse throws a ZodError, which is not an AppError, so executeRoute's catch returns the generic 500, without logging it.

items.prompt: An operator tries to move their PAUSED workflow back to DRAFT. What does assertValidWorkflowTransition do?

choices.text: Throws 422, as DRAFT is not a valid target status
Allows it, as PAUSED may return to any earlier status
Throws 409 INVALID_WORKFLOW_TRANSITION for the move
Allows it only when no runs have been created so far

choices: Throws 422, as DRAFT is not a valid target status
Allows it, as PAUSED may return to any earlier status
Throws 409 INVALID_WORKFLOW_TRANSITION for the move
Allows it only when no runs have been created so far

items.explanation: allowedTransitions lists PAUSED: [ACTIVE, ARCHIVED]. A same-state request returns early, but PAUSED to DRAFT is not allowed and throws 409.

items.prompt: An ANALYST sends PATCH /api/workflows/:id with a body that would also fail schema validation. Which status comes back?

choices.text: 500, as the ZodError from the body is caught as unknown
403 FORBIDDEN, because the permission check runs first
400 with the list of field errors from the schema parse
404 WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, as analysts see no workflows

choices: 500, as the ZodError from the body is caught as unknown
403 FORBIDDEN, because the permission check runs first
400 with the list of field errors from the schema parse
404 WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, as analysts see no workflows

items.explanation: executeRoute asserts the route permission before it parses the body, and workflow:write is not in the analyst matrix, so the AppError(403) is thrown first.

items.prompt: Operator A posts order.created to /api/events/ingest. Operator B owns an ACTIVE EVENT workflow listening for order.created; A cannot see it. What happens to B's workflow?

choices.text: Nothing, as B's workflow answers 404 for A, as a manual run does
It gets a run too, as event matching ignores the caller's scope
Nothing, as the ingest only matches the caller's workflows
It gets a run only if A has been made an admin or an analyst

choices: Nothing, as B's workflow answers 404 for A, as a manual run does
It gets a run too, as event matching ignores the caller's scope
Nothing, as the ingest only matches the caller's workflows
It gets a run only if A has been made an admin or an analyst

items.explanation: The ingest route requires only workflow:execute, which OPERATOR has, and passes the actor along (ingest/route.ts:6-10). ingestEvent calls listActiveEventWorkflows(eventName) (workflow-dispatch-service.ts:62-68), whose where clause is just ACTIVE, EVENT and the event name, with no scope or owner parameter (workflow-repository.ts:170-183). Every matching workflow in the system gets a run, B's included, and the run is credited to A. The manual trigger path loads the workflow through the caller's visibility scope first; the event path never does. Authorization sits on that read path but not on the event fan-out.

items.prompt: An operator clicks Trigger in the builder; the run is created QUEUED and the worker finishes it 5 s later. The operator then watches the page for two minutes without clicking anything. What does the run's badge show?

choices.text: SUCCEEDED, as the runs query polls every 30 seconds
RUNNING, as the badge follows the step that is active
QUEUED, as nothing refetches the runs after the trigger
SUCCEEDED, as the worker pushes the change to the page

choices: SUCCEEDED, as the runs query polls every 30 seconds
RUNNING, as the badge follows the step that is active
QUEUED, as nothing refetches the runs after the trigger
SUCCEEDED, as the worker pushes the change to the page

items.explanation: A run is created QUEUED (workflow-run-repository.ts:39-48). The trigger mutation then invalidates ["workflow-runs", id] once (workflow-builder.tsx:161-171), so the panel fetches the run while it is still QUEUED. After that the runs query has no refetchInterval (use-workflow.ts:14-20), the client sets refetchOnWindowFocus false and a 30 s staleTime (app-providers.tsx:8-17), and there is no socket or server push. Staleness never starts a request by itself: only a mount, a network reconnect or an invalidation does, and none happens while the operator watches. So the badge stays QUEUED until the page remounts or another mutation invalidates the key. A refetchInterval while any run is QUEUED or RUNNING would fix it.

items.prompt: The most recently updated workflow on an operator's dashboard has 50,000 runs. To build the dashboard's recentRuns list of eight, how many of that workflow's runs does the server load?

choices.text: All 50,000, before it sorts in memory and keeps eight
Five, the newest runs that listWorkflows already loads
Eight, as the run query takes the newest eight rows
Two, its fair share of the eight after the merge step

choices: All 50,000, before it sorts in memory and keeps eight
Five, the newest runs that listWorkflows already loads
Eight, as the run query takes the newest eight rows
Two, its fair share of the eight after the merge step

items.explanation: getDashboard calls listRunsForWorkflow for each workflow it samples (workflow-monitoring-service.ts:22-31). That repository method has a where, an include and an orderBy, but no take (workflow-run-repository.ts:93-109), so it returns every run of the workflow. The service then flattens the four arrays, sorts them by createdAt in JavaScript and slices eight. So one busy workflow drags its whole history over the wire on every dashboard load. listWorkflows already includes the five newest runs per workflow, but the dashboard does not use them; a single query with orderBy createdAt desc and take 8 would do the job.

items.prompt: A step's HTTP URL is "https://api.test/orders/{{payload.orderId}}", but the trigger payload has no orderId. What URL is called?

choices.text: "https://api.test/orders/undefined", since the lookup returns undefined
None: the step throws a missing-variable error and enters retrying
The URL unchanged, with the literal {{payload.orderId}} placeholder
"https://api.test/orders/" with the token replaced by an empty string

choices: "https://api.test/orders/undefined", since the lookup returns undefined
None: the step throws a missing-variable error and enters retrying
The URL unchanged, with the literal {{payload.orderId}} placeholder
"https://api.test/orders/" with the token replaced by an empty string

items.explanation: lookupToken returns "" for a segment that is not present, and resolveTemplateStrings substitutes String(""), so the placeholder disappears and the request goes to /orders/.

items.prompt: A step has maxRetries 2 and its HTTP action throws every time. How often does it run, and what waits come between the attempts?

choices.text: Two attempts, with one wait of 15 s in between
Two retries after the first try, each after 30 s
Four attempts, waiting 15 s, 30 s and then 45 s
Three attempts, with waits of 15 s and then 30 s

choices: Two attempts, with one wait of 15 s in between
Two retries after the first try, each after 30 s
Four attempts, waiting 15 s, 30 s and then 45 s
Three attempts, with waits of 15 s and then 30 s

items.explanation: The job's maxAttempts is maxRetries + 1 = 3. On failure readyAt is now + attempts * 15 000 ms, so 15 s after the first failure and 30 s after the second; the third failure marks the step failed and the job dead.

items.prompt: An event matches three workflows. Creating the third workflow's run fails with a database error, and the client retries the same event. How many runs do the first two workflows end up with?

choices.text: One each, as the whole ingest ran in a single transaction
None, as the failure rolls back every run of that event
One each, as the retry is deduplicated by the event name
Two each, as their first runs committed before the failure

choices: One each, as the whole ingest ran in a single transaction
None, as the failure rolls back every run of that event
One each, as the retry is deduplicated by the event name
Two each, as their first runs committed before the failure

items.explanation: ingestEvent loops over the matched workflows and, for each one, awaits createRunForWorkflow and then writes a workflow.event.dispatched audit row (workflow-dispatch-service.ts:66-79). Each createRunForWorkflow is its own $transaction (workflow-run-repository.ts:37-90), so runs one and two are committed before the third is attempted. The third failure propagates out of the loop and executeRoute answers 500, but nothing undoes the earlier runs. The event carries no idempotency key and nothing records that it was processed, so the retry matches all three workflows again and enqueues new runs for the first two. One transaction around the fan-out, or an event id stored under a unique key, would make the retry safe.

items.prompt: Operator B manually triggers an ACTIVE workflow that operator A created. What does the dispatch service return?

choices.text: 404 WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, as operators only see their own
409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE for another owner's workflow
403 WORKFLOW_SCOPE_VIOLATION from the ownership check itself
201, as any operator may trigger an active workflow

choices: 404 WORKFLOW_NOT_FOUND, as operators only see their own
409 WORKFLOW_NOT_ACTIVE for another owner's workflow
403 WORKFLOW_SCOPE_VIOLATION from the ownership check itself
201, as any operator may trigger an active workflow

items.explanation: findById applies the "own" visibility scope for operators, so the workflow is not found and the 404 is thrown before assertCanManageWorkflow is ever reached.

items.prompt: An operator owns six workflows. The one updated longest ago has failed 20 times today; the other five have no failures. How many does the Recent Failures tile count from that workflow?

choices.text: None, as only the four latest-updated workflows count
All 20, as the tile counts every failed run of the day
Eight, as the tile caps the count at the list length
Five, the failures among its five newest included runs

choices: None, as only the four latest-updated workflows count
All 20, as the tile counts every failed run of the day
Eight, as the tile caps the count at the list length
Five, the failures among its five newest included runs

items.explanation: The tile shows stats.failedRuns (workflow-dashboard.tsx:49), and that number counts FAILED runs inside recentRuns only (workflow-monitoring-service.ts:40). recentRuns is built from the runs of the first four workflows, which listWorkflows orders by updatedAt descending (workflow-monitoring-service.ts:24-25), so a workflow outside the four most recently updated contributes nothing, however often it fails. Even inside the four, only the eight newest runs are counted. The tile is therefore a count over a display sample, not a failure metric; a separate count query filtered by status and time would be.

items.prompt: In the builder, an operator changes the cron expression of an ACTIVE scheduled workflow but does not save. They click Move to PAUSED and the pause succeeds. What does the cron field show afterwards?

choices.text: The edited cron, as the form sync only runs on the first load
The edited cron, as unsaved form state is kept apart
The saved cron again, as the refetch re-runs the form sync
The edited cron, now saved along with the status change

choices: The edited cron, as the form sync only runs on the first load
The edited cron, as unsaved form state is kept apart
The saved cron again, as the refetch re-runs the form sync
The edited cron, now saved along with the status change

items.explanation: The status mutation invalidates ["workflow", id] on success (workflow-builder.tsx:155-158), so the workflow is refetched. The builder copies server data into its form state in a useEffect keyed on workflowQuery.data (workflow-builder.tsx:79-101), and the refetched workflow differs (its status is now PAUSED), so React Query hands back a new data object and the effect runs, overwriting name, cron, event name and steps with the saved values. A probe with @tanstack/query-core 5.73.3 (the package.json floor) returned the same reference for an identical refetch and a new one after a status change. The publish request carries only the status, so the edit is not saved anywhere, and the effect has no first-load-only guard.

items.prompt: An ANALYST and an OPERATOR who created no workflows both call GET /api/workflows. What do they each see?

choices.text: The analyst sees every workflow; the operator sees none
Neither sees any, as both of them created nothing
The operator sees every workflow; the analyst sees shared ones
Both see every workflow, as reads are open to all

choices: The analyst sees every workflow; the operator sees none
Neither sees any, as both of them created nothing
The operator sees every workflow; the analyst sees shared ones
Both see every workflow, as reads are open to all

items.explanation: getWorkflowVisibilityScope returns "all" for ADMIN and ANALYST and "own" for OPERATOR, so a read-only analyst sees more than an operator does.

items.prompt: An operator clicks Move to ACTIVE on a draft, and the publish request comes back 422 with a readiness message. What does the builder show?

choices.text: A generic Request failed. message above the status buttons
No message, as nothing renders the status mutation error
The readiness message, under the Trigger workflow button
The readiness message, in the form's red error line

choices: A generic Request failed. message above the status buttons
No message, as nothing renders the status mutation error
The readiness message, under the Trigger workflow button
The readiness message, in the form's red error line

items.explanation: apiRequest turns the 422 into a thrown Error carrying the server's message (api-client.ts:10-14), so the status mutation does fail. But that mutation has only an onSuccess (workflow-builder.tsx:149-159): no onError sets formError, and nothing in the JSX reads statusMutation.error. The red line renders formError, which only the save mutation's onError sets (workflow-builder.tsx:292), and the message under the Trigger button reads triggerMutation.error. The status buttons (workflow-builder.tsx:297-301) just call mutate, so the click appears to do nothing and the workflow stays DRAFT.

items.prompt: An operator manually triggers their own ACTIVE workflow whose trigger type is SCHEDULE. What happens?

choices.text: A run is queued with triggerSource "manual" and 201
A run is queued, and nextScheduledAt moves ahead
422, since a manual run needs an event name to be set
409, since scheduled workflows are started by cron alone

choices: A run is queued with triggerSource "manual" and 201
A run is queued, and nextScheduledAt moves ahead
422, since a manual run needs an event name to be set
409, since scheduled workflows are started by cron alone

items.explanation: triggerWorkflowManually checks only that the workflow is ACTIVE; it never looks at triggerType. It enqueues with source "manual" and does not touch nextScheduledAt.

items.prompt: An operator renames their own ACTIVE workflow, which has already run twice, and saves the form unchanged otherwise. What does PATCH /api/workflows/:id return?

choices.text: 409, as a workflow that has runs is locked from edits
200, with new steps and the old runs' history deleted
500, as the activation re-check rejects the edited workflow
500, as deleting its steps hits a Restrict foreign key

choices: 409, as a workflow that has runs is locked from edits
200, with new steps and the old runs' history deleted
500, as the activation re-check rejects the edited workflow
500, as deleting its steps hits a Restrict foreign key

items.explanation: updateWorkflow replaces the steps wholesale: inside a transaction it calls tx.workflowStep.deleteMany({ where: { workflowId } }) and then recreates them (workflow-repository.ts:134-136 and on). Every run left WorkflowStepRun rows that point at the old steps, and that relation is onDelete: Restrict (schema.prisma:160), so PostgreSQL refuses the delete and the whole transaction rolls back. Prisma's error is not an AppError, so executeRoute answers 500 with its generic message (route-helpers.ts:48-62). A probe with Prisma 6.19.3 (package.json allows ^6.6.0; there is no lockfile) on PostgreSQL 18 rejected the same deleteMany with a foreign-key error and left the steps untouched. The activation re-check passes for a rename, and when it does fail it throws a 422 AppError (workflow-definition-service.ts:84-87), not a 500. Nothing cascades the history away or returns 409; in effect a workflow that has run can no longer be edited.
